# Instruments: Suona (唢呐): middle, big and small

A note's `pitch` uses the **MIDI pitch (60 = middle C)**. The other Chinese instruments and the note fields they share: [../chinese.md](../chinese.md).

| instrument | Recommended range | Polyphony | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `yinse.blow.suona` | 67–95 | 1 | Suona (唢呐): the loud double-reed horn with a brass bell, bright, nasal and raspy, a wide vibrato; weddings, festivals, 百鸟朝凤; one note at a time, overlapping notes slur, `scoop` / `fall` slide in from below and drop off the end |
| `yinse.blow.suona_big` | 55–84 | 1 | Big suona (大唢呐): longer, with a big bell, a fourth or fifth below the suona; thick, rough and full, more low-mids; northern folk bands, weddings and funerals, opera accompaniment |
| `yinse.blow.haidi` | 79–103 | 1 | Haidi (海笛, the small suona): short, with a tiny reed, a fourth to an octave above the suona; shrill, thin and the brightest, for bird calls and ornate high lines |

## Adjustable parameters (instrument_params)

Override the sound of the chosen instrument/preset; write only the items you want to change, the rest stay as they are. `muser instruments <name>` shows the preset's current values.

| Parameter | Range | Automation | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `membrane` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | The dizi's membrane (笛膜): 0 none, a plain flute; 0.6 the bright, buzzing dizi sound; 1 a loud buzz. Louder notes buzz more |
| `attack` | 0.002 – 1 s | next note | Breath build-up: short = clear tonguing; long = soft entry |
| `release` | 0.005 – 2 s | next note | Wind-down time after release |
| `vibrato_rate` | 0 – 12 Hz | next note | Breath vibrato rate (5-6) |
| `vibrato_depth` | 0 – 100 cent | next note | Vibrato depth: 0 straight; 10-20 normal; 30+ the wide folk vibrato |
| `vibrato_delay` | 0 – 4 s | next note | Delay after a note starts before the vibrato |
| `breath_noise` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | Breath noise: more airflow |
| `breath` | 0.3 – 1.5 | ✓ | Breath strength (气息): scales how hard the player blows; 1 as preset, 0.6 a soft, airy, darker breath, 1.3 a full, bright one. Automate it to shape a phrase |
| `embouchure` | 0.05 – 1 | ✓ | Embouchure (口型): how far the lips let the air through; smaller is darker and softer, larger is fuller and brighter |
| `articulation` | 0 – 1 | next note | Tonguing (舌法): how hard the tongue starts a note, 0 soft (legato-like), 1 a hard, clear attack with more chiff (staccato) |
| `rasp` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | Rasp (沙哑): noise that rides on every cycle of the wave, the irregular beating of a reed; 0 clean, 0.35 the suona's grain, 0.8 a hoarse, cracking tone (automate it for a 破音 effect) |
| `width` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | Width: a few very close reflections, different left and right, as if played in a room; the sound gets breadth without a reverb's tail. 0 a dry, centred source |
| `drone` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | Drone pipe (附管, the hulusi's side pipes): how loud the held note under the melody is, sounding while the player blows; 0 off (stopped), 0.3 a soft drone |
| `drone_note` | 24 – 108 (integer) | — | The drone pipe's note (MIDI): usually the key's tonic or fifth (72 = C5 on a C hulusi) |
| `breath_vibrato` | 0 – 1 | next note | Breath vibrato (气震音): how much the vibrato also swells the breath, louder and softer at `vibrato_rate`; 0.25 a little, 0.8 the pulsing breath vibrato (with a small `vibrato_depth` it is almost only in the breath) |
| `tone` | 500 – 20000 Hz | ✓ | Final low-pass: brightness |

Automation column: ✓ = notes already sounding follow immediately; next note = affects only notes that start afterward; — = cannot be automated. See [automation.md](../../automation.md).

## Tips and common mistakes

- The loud double-reed horn with a brass bell: bright, nasal and raspy (its energy sits at 1.6-4 kHz), made for weddings, festivals and processions; it carries over a whole band, so give it the melody and keep the rest lighter. Three sizes: `yinse.blow.suona` (the middle one, G4-B6, melodies mostly A4-D6), `yinse.blow.suona_big` (大唢呐, a fourth or fifth lower, G3-C6: thick, rough, more low-mids, for northern folk bands, weddings, funerals and opera accompaniment) and `yinse.blow.haidi` (海笛, the small suona, G5-G7: shrill, thin and the brightest, for bird calls and ornate high lines). All three get sharper and rougher as they climb, as real ones do.
- **Slides are its speech**: most held notes scoop up into their pitch or fall off the end. `"scoop": 1` (0-2 semitones) starts the note below and slides up in about 0.12 s; `"fall": 1.5` drops the last 0.15 s; for wider swoops write a `bend`. `"slide": true` on an overlapping note glides from the previous one.
- **Wide vibrato**: about ±30-40 cents at 5-6 Hz on long notes, by itself (`vibrato_depth`); 50+ for the singing, crying style of 豫剧 and northern pieces.
- **Ornaments, very many**: in solo recordings half the notes are shorter than 70 ms. 叠音 (an upper flick just before a note), 打音 (a lower flick inside a held note), 历音 (a quick run up into a note), 颤音 `"trill": true`, written as on the dizi (see [dizi.md](dizi.md) for timings).
- **Tongue**: 吐音 single, double and triple tonguing as quick short notes with small gaps; `"flutter": true` is 花舌, common in lively pieces; `accent` is a hard tongued attack.
- **Bird calls (百鸟朝凤)**: fast upward chirps: very short notes with a `bend` rising one or two semitones, in quick groups, and trills high up.
- **Grain**: `rasp` (0.35 by default) is the noise riding on each cycle of the reed, the suona's grain; 0.15 a smoother, sweeter suona, 0.7-0.9 hoarse and cracking (破音), worth automating up on a climax or a shouted note. `membrane` (the bell's bright buzz) and `breath` (气息), `embouchure` (口型) shape the tone as on the flutes.
